public_rationale: He says flatly that demand for AI software and AI add-ons 'is not there'. Company disclosures from the period show large paid demand. Microsoft reported over 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats at the end of June 2026 (e1). Salesforce reported over $1.5B of Agentforce annual recurring revenue (ARR), up more than 240% year over year, for the quarter ended July 2026 (e2). Both are AI add-ons sold with existing software, the category he names. A standalone AI coding tool, Cursor, was reported above a $2B run rate earlier in the year (e3, context). His fair point is that demand may be small next to AI spending, but that is not what these words say. Under their plain meaning, the claim is contradicted.
limitations: Both companies' figures are unaudited, and Salesforce widened its ARR definition this quarter.
Paid seats may include discounted deals, so revenue depth is unknown.
The result depends on reading 'not there' as absent demand rather than demand too small for the investment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is no real demand for AI-powered software or AI add-ons to other software.

statement.excerpt: To be explicit: the demand for AI-powered software is not there, and neither is the demand for selling AI-powered add-ons to other software.

from_speaker: the demand for AI-powered software is not there
neither is the demand for selling AI-powered add-ons to other software
if Microsoft is struggling to sell AI-powered software attached to the literally-most-used enterprise software
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, there was no substantial paying customer demand for AI-powered software products or for AI add-ons sold with existing software.
He named no period. The test uses the latest quarters companies could report on around the post: April 2026 to the post date.
Large paid adoption figures, with seats or recurring revenue in the millions or billions and growing, would show demand 'is there'.
He may have meant demand too small to justify AI capex. That reading is noted but not adopted, because his words are absolute.
criteria.support_condition: Leading AI software products and AI add-ons show little paid uptake: small, flat or falling paid seats or recurring revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Major AI add-ons and AI software products show large and growing paid adoption in the period, such as tens of millions of paid seats or billions in recurring revenue.
